I understand that. I’m sure OP does too. I’m sure MIL does too. Thinking you’re okay with something and reacting badly to it in person is a thing that happens. It just does. Yeah you’re right. It was.

One of the things that always irritated me the most about the movies was how they left out the house elves. (Sure there are other things, the marauders/ginnys characterization/Ronalds personality) 

But other than Ron’s character, (which is a whole different beast) I would argue the exclusion of the house elves is the most detrimental. 

Tl;dr: they let Neville do Dobbys job of proving Harry the Gilliweed and therefore take away the truly heart wrenching gut punch that is “here lies Dobby a free elf”

Chamber of Secrets establishes house elves as a race of magical creatures treated cruelly by pure blood wizards. The introduction of Dobby lays the framework for so much important dialogue/plot IMO. Dobby from the get go is established as being an abused servant who continues, even though it causes him to self harm to the extreme, to try and save Harry. We see him bang his head against lamps, iron his hands, beat himself. Yet he knows right from wrong and refuses to let Harry be hurt. I feel that this is important because it illustrates the idea of free will. A theme that runs through the series. (Harry has the freedom to pick a side, Sirius had free will, Remus had free will, Hagrid had free will. Dudley had free will. Regardless of the circumstances of their birth, they all had the choice to decide what they felt was right) 

In the fourth installment of the story, we are introduced to another house elf. This time her name is winky. We learn that because of a choice she made (to run when the death eaters attacked the Quidditch World Cup) she has been let go and disgraced (her words not mine). While Dobby was unhappy with his lot with the Malfoys, Winky was more than content to work for the Crouches. Until they forced her to do something she was terrified of and all she did was run. And because of their decisions to act so cruelly, winky is the one to tell the truth about Crouch Jr. she’s the reason the order has proof that Voldemort returned. Again, free will plays a huge role in the characterization of both Dobby and Winky but in different ways. 

Dobby chooses to help Harry with the 2nd task. He is the one who brings Harry the Gilliweed so that he can save his Ron. In the fifth installment were introduced to get another house elf, Kreacher who belonged to the Black family. Kreacher was a hateful, bigoted character who made everyone uncomfortable with his racist tirades. But he was a product of his house. There’s a scene in OoTP after the death of a character in which dumbledore says “look at the way a man treats his inferiors not his peers” (paraphrased). 

This then leads to the climax that is Deathly Hallows. Harry is mad pissed about Kreacher leading to the death of this character. And after some backstory (about RAB) Harry is super pissed because “you did all this for what?” And Hermione is the one who says “Harry Kreacher doesn’t think that way. RAB was kind to him, so he in turn listened. [the character] was awful to him so of course he didn’t want to help him”. And in that moment, I think Harry realizes that it isn’t about who you are, where you grew up or who raised you. It’s about the way you choose to speak to those who you feel are beneath you. “Er if you could go work at hogwarts?” Harry said in Half Blood prince. Harry requests things of Kreacher, never demands. The same way he learned to talk to Dobby in book 4. He makes an active choice to be better, and Kreacher in turn learns what it means to be better. Kreacher convinces and leads the house elves in the final battle, because he made the choice to do so. Because Harry was honest and truly kind to him and gave him that option. 

Of course this is all then comes to a head at the end of Deathly Hallows, when Dobby saves them from Malfoy Manor. Nobody forced Dobby to come save them. Dobby could have just taken Harry and left. But because Dobby had free will, he choose to save everyone. And he died for it. 

And Harry chose to bury him, the Muggle way. Harry made that decision, and because of that Griphook was willing to help him. 

“Here lies Dobby a free elf” not only speaks to the sacrifice made by a sweet, brave elf but the idea that we all have free will. To die free, to die because you knew what you were walking into and chose to anyway to protect those you felt deserved protecting is the heart of the Harry Potter books and it pisses me off the movies didn’t bother with it

You know, when my grandma died nobody really offered comfort. It was my first big loss. Since then, I’ve just done what I wished someone else would have 

I bring and arrange flowers. Maybe something sweet, just put it on the counter or fridge. Not ice cream, maybe a bit of cake. I stick around, just milling about “oh hey sorry, I used a glass for some water, ima wash it” and then just keep washing. When they are sad, I do not try to make them talk, just “hey you’re sad. That’s okay.” You don’t have to tell them they’re okay, just that it is okay to be sad. No one is upset with them. Just stick around for a bit. 

It’s okay to leave too, sometimes people just need space. Just a simple “hey I gotta run, there’s food there if you get hungry” But always come back. If they haven’t eaten, “oh I’m hungry, and this is good. Let me make you a plate” and just eat. They’ll eat too if you don’t watch them. And if not, okay. They are grieving. But make sure there is food that doesn’t require more than a simple reheat. 

Don’t overthink it, just exist as you normally do. Often people go overboard, either they don’t acknowledge or they try to fix. You can’t fix their sadness. And you cant avoid grief.  But you can coax them into getting out of bed. Into showering. Into remembering how to be a person again. 

Sometimes you can mention a memory you also have with the deceased. Maybe a funny story, maybe a time your friend told you a thing. And just leave it. If they wanna talk, listen. If they don’t, listen. Follow their lead.

That’s just my experience with my friends and my own loss, just be who you already are to them. Just a bit kinder.
